evidence.exact_quote: - **NFR-001 (P0):** Rendering a 10,000-row report completes within 2 seconds on the staging database — measured by the existing `render` timing log
| 2 | No caller other than `render` reads pricing fields directly | A hidden caller breaks when fields move | grep for `unit_price` outside src/reports.js | Phase 1 | Dana | verified |

reasoning: Two named measurements do not exercise the property their requirement states. NFR-001 requires that a 10,000-row report renders within 2 seconds on staging and names the existing render timing log as the measurement. A passive log records the duration of renders that happen to occur; it neither generates a 10,000-row report nor asserts a threshold, so if no report of that size is rendered on staging the log stays silent and the requirement is never exercised while still appearing measured. Assumption 2 states that no caller other than render reads pricing fields directly and is marked verified on the strength of a grep for unit_price outside src/reports.js. That check covers one field name and only literal textual reads: it would miss any other pricing field, dynamic access such as row indexed by a variable, destructuring under an alias, and reads through an ORM or a query built at runtime. The assumption is recorded as verified on a check narrower than the claim, which is the more dangerous of the two because it has already been marked closed.
